rationale: Mara Voss as a rare-esper combat medic in cyberarmor: a bone-ceramic medic cross stencilled on the pauldron, an esper eye-gem burned into the chest plate, an arc-scalpel with a plasma cutting edge, and a levitating esper orb with two orbiting shards over her open right hand. Twenty colours. The palette is deliberately bi-polar: a cold violet-grey armour ramp (#2a2637 -> #9a95b0) over plum-black ink #120b10, warmed only by oxide leather (belt, boot cuffs, hip ampoule pouch) and skin. The single character-local accent is arc-cyan (#1b4f5e / #3fa8bd / #b9f6ff), spent on exactly five things - visor, crest gem, respirator slot, chest sigil, blade edge, plus the floating orb - about 10% of filled pixels. No magenta, no chartreuse. Occupied box is rows 2-61 (60px) with an 18px head = 3.33 heads tall; oversized head, oversized fist, and a blade that runs from the belt to the ankle. Composition is deliberately asymmetric so the silhouette is not a rectangle: heavy dark blade wedge low-left, glowing orb and shards high-right, staggered stance with the viewer-right foot a row forward. What it sacrifices: the arc-scalpel wins the "obvious weapon" fight over subtler medic-gear reads, so the medic identity rests on the shoulder cross, the belt vials and the hip pouch rather than on a syringe silhouette. The armour is also intentionally low-chroma and near-monochrome, which makes it moody but means it carries almost no colour information at distance - the cyan does all the identification work.
frontFacingCue: Three stacked horizontal value bands on a strong vertical centre axis. The helmet dome is mid-value violet; directly under it a solid 26px ink brow (row 10) reads as an overhanging visor lip; under that a full-width cyan visor (rows 11-13) split dead centre by a 4px dark nose bridge, which forces the two eye clusters to read as a symmetrical pair rather than a profile band. Below the visor the value drops again into a warm skin cheek band (rows 15-17) with a dark metal respirator bar across the mouth carrying its own small cyan slot on the centre line, then a skin chin. The centre axis is reinforced top to bottom by the raised helmet crest (ink seams at x21/x26, bright ridge at x22-x25) with the esper gem inset in it, the nose bridge, the respirator slot, and the chest eye-gem - four centred features on the same column. Head/shoulder separation is a genuine neck: the chin is 8px wide, the neck pinches to 6px for two rows in near-black undersuit, the gorget is deliberately DARK (row 22) and the collar behind it is dark too, so the head sits in front of a shadow trough instead of merging into the 30px pauldrons. Nothing rises above the shoulder line except the head - the comm-pod is a 3px nub at the temple and the floating shards sit far right at x42-x46, well clear of the skull.
smallCheck: Survives, with caveats. Box-downscaled to 28px tall (21x28) the read order that remains is: dark helmet mass, bright cyan visor bar with its dark centre notch still visible, the neck shadow gap, wide shoulders, a cyan dot at the chest, the cyan orb cluster off the right hand, and a thin cyan diagonal where the blade edge is. That is enough to say "armoured figure facing me, cyan-eyed, holding something glowing" - the front-facing requirement holds at 28px, and it holds because the visor is 3 rows tall and full width rather than a 1px slit. What is lost: the respirator, the skin cheeks, the bandolier strap, the pauldron medic cross, the belt buckle, the hip pouch and the boot toecaps all collapse into texture, and the staggered stance flattens. The figure also reads noticeably dark at that size - the violet armour has too little value spread to survive averaging, so the sprite becomes "dark blob with cyan highlights". If 28px is the shipping size I would want a second pass that lightens the armour base one more step and thickens the neck shadow by a row; at 48px and above it is comfortable.
